IS-IS configuration on R1 and R2 also appears to be correct based on the `frr running-config` output. However, the ping from PC1 to PC2 failed. This suggests that either IS-IS adjacencies are not forming, or routes are not being advertised/learned correctly. My next step is to verify the IS-IS neighbor status on R1 to ensure the routing protocol is operational.

The previous attempt to check IS-IS IPv6 neighbors failed due to an incorrect command. I will try a more general `show isis neighbor` command within `vtysh` to see if any IS-IS adjacencies are formed. This will help diagnose why PC1 cannot reach PC2.

My previous attempts to use `vtysh -c "show isis neighbor"` on R1 failed with "Read-only command not allowed". This suggests an issue with how `vtysh` show commands are being executed in this environment. Instead of debugging `vtysh` command execution, I will directly check the IPv6 routing table on R1 using `ip -6 route` to see if it has learned the route to PC2's subnet (`2001:db8:2::/64`) via IS-IS. This will confirm if IS-IS is functioning and advertising routes.
